  • The score row reads STALE by file time only. The ship-time FIG injection re-rendered frames byte-identical to the scored ones, so the panel's score describes the shipped pixels.
  • Frame 9 no longer prints the comptroller's comment email, because house_style_check refuses a contact address on the site and the dek is the slide's alt text. A maintainer proposal to admit it is in UPGRADE_BACKLOG.md.
  • The art director's audition took ten readings of frame 5 and three later rechecks. Frame 5 changed representation to the two years its dek names, because six true-scale stacks can't fill the frame.
  • Several slide artists ran past their render caps, and the concept rebuild round became a repair round on the critics' fixes.
  • The PUCT, CourtListener and Tribune discovery polls were not run, and the craft refresh (Phase 1) was skipped.
  • The boundary re-measure fetched three cited pages before consulting the crawl boundary. No response was used and the script was corrected.
  • Effort read medium at wake, so effortLevel high in .claude/settings.json is still not taking.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

1. The post copy

Does Texas tax AI as data processing?

Comptroller Don Huffines says the Legislature never taxed AI. His proposed Rule 3.308 amendments would class cloud, AI and quantum computing as hosted technology services, outside the tax.

The release says it saves Texans money. His fiscal note has the state losing $1,947,310,000 in fiscal 2027 and $4,286,040,000 in 2032. It has local governments losing $507,450,000 in 2027 and $1,116,890,000 in 2032. The note calls the economic effect "insignificant".

Nothing is adopted yet. Comments to Robin Robinson must arrive by December 20th, the earliest adoption date.

The deck stacks the estimate, one sheet per million dollars.

Comptroller-elect Sarah Eckhardt takes over January 1st. She asked him to halt rule changes begun since August 1st. Does this one survive the handover?

#TexasComptroller #SalesTax #TexasRegister

The Grid Watch page still shows its advisory for November 1st, presentation only. The deck. Carousel no. 89 on the comptroller's proposed Rule 3.308 amendments. Three panel rounds, 7.604, 7.674 and 7.722, no hard fail in any round. Frame 5 shows the fiscal 2027 and 2032 stacks at a measured on-screen ratio of 2.2013, the true sheet ratio. Left for the next run, from the round 3 judges. The caption says the Legislature never taxed AI where the source says it did not. Frame 7 capitalises a quoted word and credits the chief revenue estimator from a paraphrase. Frame 9 offers mail with no address. The release headline quoted in c1 differs from its url and should be re-read. The weekly machine pass ran before the merge. Six maintainer proposals are in UPGRADE_BACKLOG.md under November 27th, the render report race and the comment address first. Prompt audit, taken just before the merge, which is the last point a committed payload can carry it. prompt audit: 2653 tool call(s) measured, 73 WAITED ON A HUMAN. The longest wait was 29.7 seconds, on a Bash call.
